newsitem.title: USA: Humana hits new yr-high on Physician deal.
newsitem.headline: Humana hits new yr-high on Physician deal.

text.p: Shares in managed health-care provider Humana Inc climbed to a 12-month high Tuesday as investors gave the nod to the company's $400 million acquisition of Physician Corp of America.

"It is a fabulous bargain," said National Securities Corp analyst Michael LeConey of the widely expected $7 per share friendly bid. The total value of the transaction includes assumption of $130 million in Physician Corp debt.
In late morning trade, Humana shares were up 2.7 percent, or 5/8, to 23-7/8, easing off the new 12-month peak of 24-1/8 hit earlier in the day. The previous high was 23-1/2.
"The bottom line is PCAM wanted to sell and Humana is an opportunistic buyer," he said.
A trader said, "This is not news, they (Physician Corp) said yesterday it was in talks" regarding a possible takeover of the company for $7 per share.
Physician Corp shares were up six percent, or 3/8, to 6-5/8 in late morning Nasdaq activity.
Yesterday, Physican shares fell 7/8 to 6-1/4 while Humana rose 1/2 to 23-1/4.
The news comes almost three months after Sierra Health Services Inc said it terminated its stock-swap merger agreement with Physician Corp of America.

Sierra then said it was re-evaluating the proposed merger since February 20, when Physician said it would take significant additional charges in the 1996 fourth quarter to cover increased liabilities at its workers' compensation unit.
The Sierra/Physician deal, unveiled in November, called for exchange of 0.45 Sierra shares for each Physician share.

"Sierra claimed that they could not get comfortable with the potential liabilty in that entity. It (the deal) unravelled because PCAM has a workers' compensation subsidiary that had to take a number of surprise charges because of losses," said an arbitrageur who declined to be identified.
Regarding the price Humana is paying, the arb said, "This is a steal. It is a great deal for Humana."
As part of the transaction with Humana, Physician's said it agree to reinsure the troubled workers' compensation unit.
"PCAM figured out the solution to its problem is getting reinsurance on the business," LeConey said.
